title: Clinical implementation and real-world outcomes of single-port robot-assisted laparoscopic procedures at a university medical centre
summary:
According to an incidence estimate by the Robert Koch Institute, nearly 500,000 people in Germany are newly diagnosed with cancer each year. Prostate cancer accounts for approximately 20% of all new cancer diagnoses in men. Additional urogenital malignancies that represent a non-negligible proportion of new cases include testicular tumors with an incidence of around 1.6%, bladder cancer with 4.9%, and renal tumors with 4.4% (RKI 2020). Robotic-assisted surgery has become firmly established particularly within the field of urology, and the first robot-assisted radical prostatectomies in Germany were performed in the early 2000s (Binder et al. 2001). Today, robotic-assisted procedures are considered the gold standard for a broad spectrum of uro-oncological and reconstructive urological interventions (Franco et al. 2023).

Early on, a need for an even less invasive robotic operative approach—through a single local incision—became evident, enabling novel access routes (e.g., retroperitoneal and transvesical approaches), optimizing cosmetic outcomes, reducing postoperative pain, and improving rehabilitation (Kaouk et al. 2011). Due to continuous technological advances, the new single-port (SP) platform developed by the U.S. manufacturer Intuitive Surgical Inc. has been introduced into urology in recent years. Beyond early feasibility studies, the SP system is now implemented in routine clinical practice at selected Anglo-American centers (Kaouk et al. 2014). In Europe, the system has only recently become available, and University Medical Center Mainz is among the first institutions in Europe to operate such a platform.

The establishment of alternative operative access routes—such as the retroperitoneal low-anterior approach for renal interventions or the transvesical radical prostatectomy (Pellegrino et al. 2023; Mahmoud et al. 2022)—offers new advantages. Particularly for patients with multiple prior transperitoneal surgeries, the creation of extraperitoneal working spaces enables a minimally invasive approach with nearly equivalent complication risk and comparable oncological and functional outcomes (Ferguson et al. 2024). Furthermore, studies have demonstrated benefits of robotic single-port surgery over multiport techniques, such as shortened hospital stay, reduced opioid-based analgesia, and shorter duration of transurethral catheterization (Soputro et al. 2023; Abou Zeinab 2023). Given these potential advantages and the anticipated future role of single-port surgery in urological patient care, there is substantial interest in establishing SP technology in Europe (Ditonno et al. 2024).

Health Services Research
Health services research covers a broad spectrum of topics within real-world clinical practice, including the assessment of oncological outcomes, surgical learning curves, and the development of operative quality-management systems. It also evaluates whether current evidence—e.g., guideline recommendations—is implemented in practice and whether there are process-related barriers that prevent achieving optimal therapeutic outcomes (Glaeske 2014).

To optimize hospital length of stay, morbidity, and mortality in abdominal surgery, statistical process control is commonly applied through prospective data collection followed by retrospective analysis (Lima de Mendonça et al. 2024). In order to obtain an early representation of real-world performance when introducing new surgical techniques, cumulative sum (CUSUM) analysis has become well established in urology (Chan et al. 2019).

In the context of robot-assisted prostate surgery, the collection of perioperative, oncological, and functional parameters—such as surgical margin status, biochemical recurrence, and postoperative recovery of continence and potency—is of particular interest (Kaouk et al. 2020). Similarly, quality indicators for robot-assisted partial nephrectomy include the “trifecta”, margin status, ischemia time, and postoperative pain (Francavilla et al. 2022). More complex urological SP procedures, such as single-port nephroureterectomy or radical cystectomy, have so far been reported only in small case series, underscoring the urgent need for systematic collection of intraoperative parameters, hospital stay duration, postoperative complications based on the Clavien–Dindo classification, and patient outcomes (Pellegrino et al. 2022; Zhang et al. 2020).

In summary, little is currently known about the learning curve and implementation of the robotic SP platform—and its impact on surgeons and patients—within Europe. The SP system only received medical device approval for the European Union in early 2024, and thus no clinical data from European centers are available to date. The establishment of prospective databases within Europe is essential to compare oncological and functional outcomes with those reported from Anglo-American centers. Moreover, these prospectively collected data will enable analyses comparing SP systems with the company’s multiport platforms as well as robotic systems from other manufacturers.
conditions: Malignant neoplasm of kidney, except renal pelvis

interventions.name: The study nurses perform a weekly review (Thursday/Friday) of the surgical schedule to identify upcoming single-port procedures. Eligible cases are marked in the schedule under “Notes” with the entry “SP Registry Study – Inclusion”, followed by a notification email to the responsible study team memb

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Adult patients (>18 years) with a clinical indication for the use of the single-port (SP) robotic-assisted system. This includes urological malignancies such as renal cell carcinoma, urothelial carcinoma, prostate cancer, and testicular tumors. Patients undergoing reconstructive procedures in the pelvis are also eligible, for example for symptomatic cystocele, subpelvic stenosis, genital prolapse, stress urinary incontinence, or adenoma enucleation.
Exclusion criteria:
Patients without a sufficient clinical indication for the SP system are excluded from the study.
